questions: How rapidly does nominal vertical-aggregation SNR gain disappear as positive vertical correlation increases?
Can contiguous leave-part-out calibration sensitivity identify localized contamination, and what contamination remains invisible to that diagnostic?

equicorrelation.definition: rho_k = rho for every required lag; explicit synthetic family, not an inferred SPU covariance law

exponential_lag.definition: rho_k = rho^k; explicit stationary synthetic family, not an operational model

interpretation: Positive correlation monotonically reduces the precision gain of aggregation.
With strong equicorrelation rho=0.9, 60 m and 120 m gains both collapse to approximately 1.05, so doubling width yields little additional random-noise benefit while still sacrificing resolution.
The two limiting uncertainty brackets remain useful, but intermediate covariance can materially change expected gain and must not be replaced by whichever assumption gives more altitude coverage.

leave_quarter_out.definition: Fit the full nominal Rayleigh window, then recompute the origin-constrained calibration after removing each of four contiguous positional quarters; report the factor range relative to the full fit.

localized_asymmetric_contamination.finding: Localized contamination changes the fitted scale when the affected part is removed, so leave-out sensitivity can expose this failure mode.

broad_symmetric_contamination.finding: The fitted scale is biased by more than 20% while leave-quarter-out subsets remain mutually stable; leave-out agreement is therefore not a molecular-purity certificate.

decision: Keep covariance and leave-part-out as explicit diagnostic dimensions. Do not derive a universal correlation law, contamination threshold, productive aggregation width or high-column pass/fail rule from these synthetics.
next_gate: confirm cross-platform CI for the new synthetic tests
apply the same evidence/high-boundary workflow to a materially different real SPU case
retain strict support and resolution accounting before any method-v5 proposal
